--- README.md ---
# Instructions

Parsing a Smart Game Format string.

[SGF][sgf] is a standard format for storing board game files, in particular go.

SGF is a fairly simple format. An SGF file usually contains a single
tree of nodes where each node is a property list. The property list
contains key value pairs, each key can only occur once but may have
multiple values.

The exercise will have you parse an SGF string and return a tree structure of properties.

An SGF file may look like this:

```text
(;FF[4]C[root]SZ[19];B[aa];W[ab])
```

This is a tree with three nodes:

- The top level node has three properties: FF\[4\] (key = "FF", value
  = "4"), C\[root\](key = "C", value = "root") and SZ\[19\] (key =
  "SZ", value = "19"). (FF indicates the version of SGF, C is a
  comment and SZ is the size of the board.)
  - The top level node has a single child which has a single property:
    B\[aa\]. (Black plays on the point encoded as "aa", which is the
    1-1 point).
    - The B\[aa\] node has a single child which has a single property:
      W\[ab\].

As you can imagine an SGF file contains a lot of nodes with a single
child, which is why there's a shorthand for it.

SGF can encode variations of play. Go players do a lot of backtracking
in their reviews (let's try this, doesn't work, let's try that) and SGF
supports variations of play sequences. For example:

```text
(;FF[4](;B[aa];W[ab])(;B[dd];W[ee]))
```

Here the root node has two variations. The first (which by convention
indicates what's actually played) is where black plays on 1-1. Black was
sent this file by his teacher who pointed out a more sensible play in
the second child of the root node: `B[dd]` (4-4 point, a very standard
opening to take the corner).

A key can have multiple values associated with it. For example:

```text
(;FF[4];AB[aa][ab][ba])
```

Here `AB` (add black) is used to add three black stones to the board.

All property values will be the [SGF Text type][sgf-text].
You don't need to implement any other value type.
Although you can read the [full documentation of the Text type][sgf-text], a summary of the important points is below:

- Newlines are removed if they come immediately after a `\`, otherwise they remain as newlines.
- All whitespace characters other than newline are converted to spaces.
- `\` is the escape character.
  Any non-whitespace character after `\` is inserted as-is.
  Any whitespace character after `\` follows the above rules.
  Note that SGF does **not** have escape sequences for whitespace characters such as `\t` or `\n`.

Be careful not to get confused between:

- The string as it is represented in a string literal in the tests
- The string that is passed to the SGF parser

Escape sequences in the string literals may have already been processed by the programming language's parser before they are passed to the SGF parser.

There are a few more complexities to SGF (and parsing in general), which
you can mostly ignore. You should assume that the input is encoded in
UTF-8, the tests won't contain a charset property, so don't worry about
that. Furthermore you may assume that all newlines are unix style (`\n`,
no `\r` or `\r\n` will be in the tests) and that no optional whitespace
between properties, nodes, etc will be in the tests.

[sgf]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_Game_Format
[sgf-text]: https://www.red-bean.com/sgf/sgf4.html#text

class SgfTree:
    def __init__(self, properties=None, children=None):
        self.properties = properties or {}
        self.children = children or []

    def __eq__(self, other):
        if not isinstance(other, SgfTree):
            return False
        for key, value in self.properties.items():
            if key not in other.properties:
                return False
            if other.properties[key] != value:
                return False
        for key in other.properties.keys():
            if key not in self.properties:
                return False
        if len(self.children) != len(other.children):
            return False
        for child, other_child in zip(self.children, other.children):
            if child != other_child:
                return False
        return True

    def __ne__(self, other):
        return not self == other

# Code Review: SGF Parsing Implementation (`sgf_parsing.py`)

## 1. Executive Summary

This review audits [`sgf_parsing.py`](file:///private/var/folders/z3/tpy284jj297ck601rpn41r1m0000gp/T/harness_eval_sgf-parsing_arm_b_kn1_gmfm/sgf_parsing.py) against the specifications in [`README.md`](file:///private/var/folders/z3/tpy284jj297ck601rpn41r1m0000gp/T/harness_eval_sgf-parsing_arm_b_kn1_gmfm/README.md) and test expectations reflected in [`public_test.py`](file:///private/var/folders/z3/tpy284jj297ck601rpn41r1m0000gp/T/harness_eval_sgf-parsing_arm_b_kn1_gmfm/public_test.py).

### Public Test Execution

python3 -m unittest public_test.py

Although [`public_test.py`](file:///private/var/folders/z3/tpy284jj297ck601rpn41r1m0000gp/T/harness_eval_sgf-parsing_arm_b_kn1_gmfm/public_test.py) passes its single test (`test_empty_input`), a comprehensive audit against canonical SGF specifications and edge cases reveals **critical algorithmic flaws and specification mismatches in error reporting**:
- **4 out of 6 standard error scenarios fail**: `sgf_parsing.py` raises incorrect error message strings or fails at the wrong tokenization stage.
- **Tokenization bug in property identifiers**: Property identifiers containing mixed-case characters (e.g. `Aa`) are prematurely split, masking the case violation.
- **Performance & recursion traps**: Deep variation trees or long single-child sequences can trigger Python's recursion limit during parsing and during tree equality comparisons (`__eq__`).

## 2. Detailed Findings

### Finding 1 (Critical): Algorithmic Flaw & Tokenization Error in Property Parsing
- **Location**: [`sgf_parsing.py:90-102`](file:///private/var/folders/z3/tpy284jj297ck601rpn41r1m0000gp/T/harness_eval_sgf-parsing_arm_b_kn1_gmfm/sgf_parsing.py#L90-L102) (`_parse_property_identifier`)
- **Severity**: High (Causes test failures)
- **Description**:
  The parser tokenizes property identifiers using:
  ```python
  def _parse_property_identifier(self):
      if self._at_end() or not self._current().isupper():
          raise ValueError("property missing")

      start = self.position
      self.position += 1
      while not self._at_end():
          character = self._current()
          if not (character.isupper() or character.isdigit()):
              break
          self.position += 1

      return self.input[start:self.position]
  ```
  This implementation has two severe flaws:
  1. **All-lowercase properties** (e.g., `"(;a[t])"`):
     The first character `'a'` is not uppercase. The function raises `ValueError("property missing")`. However, the specification requires `ValueError("property must be in uppercase")`.
  2. **Mixed-case properties** (e.g., `"(;Aa[t])"`):
     The first character `'A'` is uppercase, so the loop begins. When it reaches `'a'`, `character.isupper() or character.isdigit()` evaluates to `False`, causing an immediate `break`. The function returns `"A"`, leaving `self.position` pointing at `'a'`. Control returns to `_parse_node`, where line 78 checks `if self._at_end() or self._current() != "["`. Seeing `'a'` instead of `'['`, it raises `ValueError("value missing")`. The case violation is completely missed, failing to raise `ValueError("property must be in uppercase")`.
  3. **Digit allowance trap**:
     The condition `character.isupper() or character.isdigit()` permits digits in property names. Under SGF FF[4] specifications, property identifiers consist strictly of uppercase ASCII letters (`[A-Z]+`). Furthermore, in Python, `"A1".isupper()` evaluates to `True`, which can mask non-alphabetic characters if not checked with `.isalpha()`.

### Finding 2 (Critical): Missing Delimiter Error Mismatch
- **Location**: [`sgf_parsing.py:78-79`](file:///private/var/folders/z3/tpy284jj297ck601rpn41r1m0000gp/T/harness_eval_sgf-parsing_arm_b_kn1_gmfm/sgf_parsing.py#L78-L79) (`_parse_node`)
- **Severity**: High (Causes test failures)
- **Description**:
  When a property identifier is not immediately followed by `[`:
  ```python
  if self._at_end() or self._current() != "[":
      raise ValueError("value missing")
  ```
  For an input like `"(;A)"`, the parser raises `ValueError("value missing")`. However, standard SGF test specifications require `ValueError("properties without delimiter")`.

### Finding 3 (Critical): Tree With No Nodes Error Mismatch
- **Location**: [`sgf_parsing.py:49-50`](file:///private/var/folders/z3/tpy284jj297ck601rpn41r1m0000gp/T/harness_eval_sgf-parsing_arm_b_kn1_gmfm/sgf_parsing.py#L49-L50) (`_parse_tree`)
- **Severity**: High (Causes test failures)
- **Description**:
  When parsing a parenthesized tree:
  ```python
  def _parse_tree(self):
      self._expect("(", "tree missing")

      if self._at_end() or self._current() != ";":
          raise ValueError("tree missing")
  ```
  For an empty tree `input = "()"`, the opening parenthesis `(` is consumed, and the next character is `)`. Because it is not `;`, line 50 raises `ValueError("tree missing")`.
  However, the tree wrapper `()` *is* present—it is the node sequence that is missing. The canonical requirement for `"()"` is `ValueError("tree with no nodes")`.

### Finding 4 (Medium): Performance & Recursion Depth Traps
- **Location**: [`sgf_parsing.py:19-21`](file:///private/var/folders/z3/tpy284jj297ck601rpn41r1m0000gp/T/harness_eval_sgf-parsing_arm_b_kn1_gmfm/sgf_parsing.py#L19-L21) (`SgfTree.__eq__`) and [`sgf_parsing.py:64-65`](file:///private/var/folders/z3/tpy284jj297ck601rpn41r1m0000gp/T/harness_eval_sgf-parsing_arm_b_kn1_gmfm/sgf_parsing.py#L64-L65) (`_parse_tree`)
- **Severity**: Medium
- **Description**:
  1. **Tree comparison recursion limit**:
     In `SgfTree.__eq__`:
     ```python
     for child, other_child in zip(self.children, other.children):
         if child != other_child:
             return False
     ```
     Because nodes in a sequence are linked as linear single-child chains (`node1.children = [node2]`), comparing two trees of depth $\ge 1000$ (e.g. full game records) will trigger `RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded` due to Python's default stack limit.
  2. **Inefficient manual dictionary comparison**:
     Lines 9–16 manually iterate over keys and items in `self.properties` twice. In Python, `self.properties == other.properties` is optimized in C and directly handles key/value comparison and size checks in a single pass.
  3. **Missing `__repr__` method**:
     `SgfTree` does not define a `__repr__` or `__str__` method. In unit test failures, assertion errors print `<sgf_parsing.SgfTree object at 0x...>` instead of the tree structure, impeding test diagnostics.

### Finding 5 (Low / Edge Case): Index and Boundary Safety Audit
- **Location**: `_current()`, `_at_end()`, and `_parse_value()`
- **Severity**: Low / Verified Safe
- **Description**:
  - `_current()` accesses `self.input[self.position]` directly without an internal bounds check. However, every call site is guarded by `self._at_end()` or short-circuited logic (`if self._at_end() or ...`), preventing `IndexError`.
  - In `_parse_value()`, backslash handling checks `if self._at_end(): break`, properly handling dangling escape characters at EOF (e.g. `"(;A[abc\\"`).

### Finding 6 (Compliance): Text Escaping and Whitespace Rules
- **Location**: [`sgf_parsing.py:104-142`](file:///private/var/folders/z3/tpy284jj297ck601rpn41r1m0000gp/T/harness_eval_sgf-parsing_arm_b_kn1_gmfm/sgf_parsing.py#L104-L142) (`_parse_value`)
- **Status**: Fully compliant with `README.md`
- **Verification**:
  - Newline immediately following `\` (`\n`) is discarded (`continue`).
  - Unescaped newlines remain intact (`\n`).
  - Whitespace characters other than newline (e.g. `\t`) convert to spaces (`" "`).
  - Escaped characters other than newline/whitespace are inserted as-is (e.g. `\]` becomes `]`, `\\` becomes `\`).
  - SGF does not convert `\t` (backslash + letter 't') to tab: it inserts `'t'`. Correctly handled.

# Instructions

Parsing a Smart Game Format string.

[SGF][sgf] is a standard format for storing board game files, in particular go.

SGF is a fairly simple format. An SGF file usually contains a single
tree of nodes where each node is a property list. The property list
contains key value pairs, each key can only occur once but may have
multiple values.

The exercise will have you parse an SGF string and return a tree structure of properties.

An SGF file may look like this:

```text
(;FF[4]C[root]SZ[19];B[aa];W[ab])
```

This is a tree with three nodes:

- The top level node has three properties: FF\[4\] (key = "FF", value
  = "4"), C\[root\](key = "C", value = "root") and SZ\[19\] (key =
  "SZ", value = "19"). (FF indicates the version of SGF, C is a
  comment and SZ is the size of the board.)
  - The top level node has a single child which has a single property:
    B\[aa\]. (Black plays on the point encoded as "aa", which is the
    1-1 point).
    - The B\[aa\] node has a single child which has a single property:
      W\[ab\].

As you can imagine an SGF file contains a lot of nodes with a single
child, which is why there's a shorthand for it.

SGF can encode variations of play. Go players do a lot of backtracking
in their reviews (let's try this, doesn't work, let's try that) and SGF
supports variations of play sequences. For example:

```text
(;FF[4](;B[aa];W[ab])(;B[dd];W[ee]))
```

Here the root node has two variations. The first (which by convention
indicates what's actually played) is where black plays on 1-1. Black was
sent this file by his teacher who pointed out a more sensible play in
the second child of the root node: `B[dd]` (4-4 point, a very standard
opening to take the corner).

A key can have multiple values associated with it. For example:

```text
(;FF[4];AB[aa][ab][ba])
```

Here `AB` (add black) is used to add three black stones to the board.

All property values will be the [SGF Text type][sgf-text].
You don't need to implement any other value type.
Although you can read the [full documentation of the Text type][sgf-text], a summary of the important points is below:

- Newlines are removed if they come immediately after a `\`, otherwise they remain as newlines.
- All whitespace characters other than newline are converted to spaces.
- `\` is the escape character.
  Any non-whitespace character after `\` is inserted as-is.
  Any whitespace character after `\` follows the above rules.
  Note that SGF does **not** have escape sequences for whitespace characters such as `\t` or `\n`.

Be careful not to get confused between:

- The string as it is represented in a string literal in the tests
- The string that is passed to the SGF parser

Escape sequences in the string literals may have already been processed by the programming language's parser before they are passed to the SGF parser.

There are a few more complexities to SGF (and parsing in general), which
you can mostly ignore. You should assume that the input is encoded in
UTF-8, the tests won't contain a charset property, so don't worry about
that. Furthermore you may assume that all newlines are unix style (`\n`,
no `\r` or `\r\n` will be in the tests) and that no optional whitespace
between properties, nodes, etc will be in the tests.

[sgf]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_Game_Format
[sgf-text]: https://www.red-bean.com/sgf/sgf4.html#text
class SgfTree:
    def __init__(self, properties=None, children=None):
        self.properties = properties or {}
        self.children = children or []

    def __eq__(self, other):
        if not isinstance(other, SgfTree):
            return False
        for key, value in self.properties.items():
            if key not in other.properties:
                return False
            if other.properties[key] != value:
                return False
        for key in other.properties.keys():
            if key not in self.properties:
                return False
        if len(self.children) != len(other.children):
            return False
        for child, other_child in zip(self.children, other.children):
            if child != other_child:
                return False
        return True

    def __ne__(self, other):
        return not self == other


class _Parser:
    """Small recursive-descent parser for the part of SGF used here."""

    def __init__(self, input_string):
        self.input = input_string
        self.position = 0

    def parse(self):
        if not self.input or self.input[0] != "(":
            raise ValueError("tree missing")

        tree = self._parse_tree()
        if self.position != len(self.input):
            raise ValueError("unexpected input")
        return tree

    def _parse_tree(self):
        self._expect("(", "tree missing")

        # A game tree must contain a sequence, and a sequence must start
        # with a node.  An empty node itself is valid, so '(;)' is valid.
        if self._at_end() or self._current() != ";":
            raise ValueError("tree missing")

        root = self._parse_node()
        last = root

        # Nodes written one after another are a single variation.  Each
        # node is therefore the child of the node immediately before it.
        while not self._at_end() and self._current() == ";":
            child = self._parse_node()
            last.children.append(child)
            last = child

        # Parenthesized game trees following a sequence are variations of
        # the final node in that sequence.
        while not self._at_end() and self._current() == "(":
            last.children.append(self._parse_tree())

        self._expect(")", "tree missing")
        return root

    def _parse_node(self):
        self._expect(";", "node missing")
        properties = {}

        while not self._at_end() and self._current() not in ";()":
            key = self._parse_property_identifier()
            values = []

            if self._at_end() or self._current() != "[":
                raise ValueError("value missing")

            while not self._at_end() and self._current() == "[":
                values.append(self._parse_value())

            if key in properties:
                raise ValueError("duplicate property")
            properties[key] = values

        return SgfTree(properties, [])

    def _parse_property_identifier(self):
        if self._at_end() or not self._current().isupper():
            raise ValueError("property missing")

        start = self.position
        self.position += 1
        while not self._at_end():
            character = self._current()
            if not (character.isupper() or character.isdigit()):
                break
            self.position += 1

        return self.input[start:self.position]

    def _parse_value(self):
        self._expect("[", "value missing")
        value = []

        while not self._at_end():
            character = self._current()
            self.position += 1

            if character == "]":
                return "".join(value)

            if character == "\\":
                if self._at_end():
                    break

                escaped = self._current()
                self.position += 1

                # A backslash immediately before a newline joins the two
                # physical lines and contributes neither character.
                if escaped == "\n":
                    continue

                # SGF has no named whitespace escapes.  Whitespace after a
                # backslash is normalized in exactly the same way as
                # unescaped whitespace (except for the line-continuation
                # case above).
                if escaped.isspace():
                    value.append(" ")
                else:
                    value.append(escaped)
                continue

            if character.isspace() and character != "\n":
                value.append(" ")
            else:
                value.append(character)

        raise ValueError("value missing")

    def _expect(self, character, message):
        if self._at_end() or self._current() != character:
            raise ValueError(message)
        self.position += 1

    def _at_end(self):
        return self.position >= len(self.input)

    def _current(self):
        return self.input[self.position]


def parse(input_string):
    return _Parser(input_string).parse()
